paragraphs.speaker: Host, Angel Chu
paragraphs.text: Finally, please help me prepare an important prop. Do you know what day it is today? Please open it and pass it down. There are two flavors — dark chocolate. Happy Valentine's Day. May everyone be happy every day. Now bless each other, left and right — wish each other a Happy Valentine's Day.

paragraphs.speaker: Host, Angel Chu
paragraphs.text: Okay, so now we'll give the time to Janet and Tim. And when I say "welcome," everyone say "Happy Valentine's Day." Welcome, Tim!

paragraphs.speaker: Audience
paragraphs.text: Happy Valentine's Day!

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Okay. I know. Now I understand — it took me a while to figure this out. Is Valentine's Day always August 19th?

paragraphs.speaker: Host
paragraphs.text: No, it's the lunar calendar — it's the lunar Valentine's Day.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So it has to do with the lunar—?

paragraphs.speaker: Host
paragraphs.text: Yeah, July 7th, the lunar. The seventh month of the lunar calendar, and the seventh day. 7-7 is Valentine's Day.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Okay, all right, cool. So — transition. So what happens on Valentine's Day? I was born in November. So if you do nine months before November... because Chinese New Year — or in the United States, we'd call it Valentine's Day. He said Chinese New Year; in the US it's Western Valentine's Day. Get it? So do you understand how I came to be? Some of you got it. So there's actually a real point to me saying this. We're going to talk about all the different ways that beings take birth. Some of you get it, some of you don't. So — Valentine's Day. What happens on Valentine's Day? Babies get made. And then nine months later, babies get born. I saw a couple more people go, "oh, I get it." But sometimes my jokes aren't that funny. Or they're just a little too American. Or people just don't get them. Anyway.

chapters.title: The Four Ways Beings Take Birth

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So the joke really is: there are four different ways that beings can be born in this system. Slide 15, Brian. They can be birthed from an egg. Next slide. They're birthed from a womb — which is a little bit different, right? In this case, the live baby is inside the mother; and in the egg version, the egg comes out and then the life forms outside of the mother. The third way, according to the Abhidharma, is that you can take birth from warmth and moisture. And this is from before they understood how mosquitoes and beings like that were born. They couldn't look microscopically and see whether there were eggs for mosquitoes in the water. So they said this type of birth is like what happens in the monsoons that are going on right now — there's a lot of water, it's warm, and then the bugs just come out. The same thing happens in Arizona too. It's dry, dry, dry, and all of a sudden there's water, and then there are mosquitoes everywhere. Which is a cool way of — this is how they observed the world.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And the fourth way, next slide. You're born as a complete being. Like a full moon, right? Meaning you just pop out as yourself — you don't have to go through birth like an egg, or a mom, or a woman. And what kinds of beings does this apply to? Actually, a lot of them — just ones we don't see. There are hell beings; the pleasure beings that are kind of above us in the desire realm; Bardo beings; the majority of the craving spirits — the hungry goats. Ghosts. Not hungry goats — ghosts. That was just a mispronunciation of English on my side. Hungry goats.

chapters.title: Beings Who Appear Complete — the Power of Karma

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Why is this important? Due to the tremendous energy of their karmic seeds — the tremendous energy coming from those past deeds — these beings don't have to go through a normal birth process. They just appear in that realm. They don't have to grow up. Each of those different types of beings, because of the tremendous energy behind it, just pops into existence. Like a hell being: the karma is so strong, they just appear there. They don't need a mother. And then they just start suffering tremendously.

chapters.title: Which Birth Causes the Least Harm

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: In general, which ones are better as types of birth? It's kind of a weird question. It depends on the karmic seed planted when you take the birth — basically, how much pain are you creating in the act of coming alive? I didn't really think about this when I taught this class about four years ago. But it's like: how much pain do you cause, for example, the person who's giving birth to you?

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So those who have this complete birth, the ones who just pop into existence — while most of those births are unfortunate, they're not actually hurting anyone. Then the next best is birth from warmth and moisture. Then, third, birth from a womb. And the worst one is birth from an egg. Why? The idea is that birth from a womb actually hurts two people. First you hurt the mother, and then you're kind of hurting yourself too.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: There's a great line in — what movie? I need to get this. There it is. It's a movie from 1989 called Look Who's Talking. It's basically a baby who talks — a funny movie. The best line from that movie, the one everyone remembers: why does giving birth hurt the mother and the baby? Okay, there are no kids here, right? "Why don't you try squeezing something the size of a watermelon out of an opening the size of a lemon, and then see how you feel?"

paragraphs.speaker: Audience
paragraphs.text: Oh, I've heard that line. Yes.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Right? So the pain of a mother giving birth is like pushing something the size of a watermelon out of a hole the size of a lemon. Just the thought of it hurts. And it hurts the baby too, because the baby's head has to go through the birth canal. Obviously the body is designed to do this — but I've seen a birth, and it's not pleasant to watch; you can just imagine how much it hurts. There's a story of Patanjali, in the Yoga Sutras, that he came out of the side of his mother, to spare his mother the pain.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: One of my friends — her baby arrived two months early, and the birth was painless. The baby had to be in the hospital for a month. But she always thought of it as a gift from the child: the child knew it was going to hurt her, so they made it painless, relatively painless. But you see, birth is not just "the miracle of life." I can't imagine what women have to go through to have children. It's a huge sacrifice to their body — the whole body changes. And the birth process is not a delight. Yes, you've created life, and there's beauty afterward. But it's also dangerous. Modern medicine has made pregnancy so much less dangerous, but it's still a risk to every woman's life to be pregnant. A friend of mine from high school died in childbirth. The baby survived; she did not. It's possible. So it's a great honor, and it's also a great risk.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And then they say the worst kind of birth is from an egg — because there's pain to the mother laying the egg. Have you ever watched a chicken lay an egg? It looks like it hurts. This thing forms inside them every couple of days, and then they have to get it out. And they say it hurts the baby on the way, in the laying of the egg. And then the hatching of the egg is another suffering. So the least amount of pain is a complete birth; the most amount of pain is the one from an egg. It's kind of this weird karma — that for humans, it's a great place to work on our karmic seeds consciously. Not to mention the nine months preparing for the birth. I'm not saying there's no beauty in it — of course there is. But there's tremendous discomfort carrying around a five-kilo baby. Is that the normal size? Hold on — I did terrible math in my head.

paragraphs.speaker: Audience
paragraphs.text: Five pounds.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Five pounds. Also the placenta — about two kilos. If you imagine five-kilo babies... all of your organs are being moved around. It's beautiful. And all the things that can go wrong, and all the things that can go right. Okay, next slide.
